new.title: See the Byzantine frescoes of Trabzon Hagia Sophia
new.desc: Built in the mid-13th century under the Komnenoi emperors of Trebizond, this cross-in-square church sits on a terrace above the sea. It became a mosque after 1461, was restored with the University of Edinburgh in 1958-62 and ran as a museum from 1964; it reopened for worship in 2013 and is open to visitors outside prayers.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly. The garden has a tea house with sea views.
new.q: Ayasofya Camii, Zübeyde Hanım Caddesi, Fatih, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Tour the Atatürk Pavilion in its pine garden
new.desc: A white villa built in the early 20th century for the Greek banker Kostaki Kabayanidis, set in pines on the Soğuksu hillside above the city. Atatürk stayed here in September 1924 and the rooms are kept with period furniture and his belongings.
new.tip: Buses leave from Atatürk Alanı about every half hour. The garden is a pleasant stroll even if the house queue is long.
new.q: Atatürk Köşkü, Soğuksu, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Browse the Trabzon Museum in the Kostaki mansion
new.desc: The museum fills a mansion built for the Greek banker Kostaki Teophylaktos on Zeytinlik Caddesi and opened as a museum on 22 April 2001. Its rooms show archaeology and Ottoman-era ethnography inside the original painted interiors.
new.tip: Allow an hour. The building is the highlight, so look up at the painted ceilings.
new.q: Trabzon Müzesi, Zeytinlik Caddesi, Kemerkaya, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Watch the city and sea from Boztepe's viewing terrace
new.desc: Boztepe is the hill that rises directly behind central Trabzon. A seyir terası and walking path give views over Ortahisar, the port and the Black Sea coast.
new.tip: Go at sunset; it is a short taxi or dolmuş ride from Atatürk Alanı.
new.q: Boztepe Seyir Terası, Boztepe, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: See the Fatih Mosque, once the Chrysokephalos church
new.desc: The mosque in the Ortahisar quarter was the major church of Trebizond, the Panaghia Chrysokephalos, converted after the 1461 Ottoman conquest. Its large Byzantine-era mass stands in the old walled core.
new.tip: Enter outside prayer times; combine with the nearby Gülbahar Hatun complex and the citadel.
new.q: Ortahisar Fatih Camii, Ortahisar Mahallesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Walk the Trabzon citadel walls above the ravines
new.desc: The walls of Trebizond's upper town run along the ridge between the Zağnos and Tabakhane ravines. Guides date the foundations to the Byzantine era, with later repairs.
new.tip: The ravine paths below the walls give the best approach; wear good shoes.
new.q: Trabzon Kalesi, Ortahisar Mahallesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Visit the Gülbahar Hatun mosque and tomb complex
new.desc: Founded in 1514 by Gülbahar Hatun, mother of Sultan Selim I, who was governor of Trabzon before taking the throne. The complex of mosque and tomb stands beside the old walls in Ortahisar.
new.tip: Open outside prayers; it is a short walk from Fatih Mosque.
new.q: Gülbahar Hatun Camii, Ortahisar Mahallesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Climb to the frescoed Kaymaklı Monastery
new.desc: Amenaperkich (Amenapırgiç) Monastery, founded in 1424 and known locally as Kaymaklı, stands on a hillside south-east of the centre. Its walls keep 18th-century frescoes, and the name recalls a milk fountain that once stood in the complex.
new.tip: Take a taxi or dolmuş towards Kaymaklı and check opening times first.
new.q: Kaymaklı Manastırı, Kaymaklı Mahallesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Stroll Zağnos Valley Park below the Zağnos bridge
new.desc: The Zağnos ravine on the western edge of the old town is crossed by an arched bridge whose earliest traces are Roman or Byzantine. The park below makes a quiet walk beside the citadel walls.
new.tip: Pair it with the citadel and Gülbahar Hatun for a half-day of old Trabzon.
new.q: Zağnos Vadisi Parkı, Zağnos Caddesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Find the cliff-carved Kızlar Monastery on Boztepe
new.desc: The Panagia Theoskepastos (Kızlar) Monastery is cut into a single rock mass on the road up Boztepe and dates to the late 14th century. Restored in recent years, it is the only monastery structure standing in the city centre.
new.tip: It sits on the Boztepe road, so stop on the way up to the terrace.
new.q: Kızlar Manastırı, Boztepe, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: See Saint Anne, Trabzon's oldest surviving church
new.desc: Küçük Ayvasıl, the Church of Saint Anne, is a small barrel-vaulted basilica near the old market quarter. It is regarded as the oldest surviving church of Trabzon, with an inscription dating it to 884-885.
new.tip: It is small and may be locked; check opening hours first.
new.q: Küçük Ayvasıl Kilisesi, Kemerkaya, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Admire the Ottoman İskender Paşa Mosque
new.desc: An Ottoman mosque on the eastern side of the old centre, named for a governor of Trabzon, and one of the city's notable Ottoman buildings.
new.tip: Easy to combine with the walk from Atatürk Alanı toward Kızlar Monastery.
new.q: İskender Paşa Camii, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Spot the Yeni Cuma Mosque by the bazaar
new.desc: The New Friday Mosque (Yeni Cuma Camii) stands close to the bazaar streets by Atatürk Alanı and serves the market district.
new.tip: Open outside prayers; a short stop between Meydan and the Bedesten.
new.q: Yeni Cuma Camii, Kemerkaya, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: See the Kanuni Ottoman Cultural House
new.desc: The building on Zağnos Caddesi is tied to Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent, born in Trabzon in 1494 while his father Selim governed. It now houses the Kanuni Sultan Süleyman Ottoman Culture House with wax figures of rulers and exhibitions.
new.tip: Check current opening hours; the Zağnos ravine is steps away.
new.q: Kanuni Evi, Zağnos Caddesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Look for the Church of Saint Gregory of Nyssa
new.desc: Nissalı Aziz Gregor Kilisesi, in the Kaledibi district, is a Byzantine church tradition links to Gregory of Nyssa. It stands near the Tomb of Solomon II in the northern part of the old city.
new.tip: Not a major draw; check access before walking over.
new.q: Nissalı Aziz Gregor Kilisesi, Zağnos Mahallesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Eat hamsi tava at Cemil Usta on Atatürk Alanı
new.desc: Cemil Usta occupies an old stone building on the north side of Meydan and is one of Trabzon's best-known restaurants. Its grill is known for fried hamsi (anchovies) in season, plus mezgit and trout.
new.tip: Order hamsi tava with mısır ekmeği in season (roughly autumn to spring).
new.q: Cemil Usta, Atatürk Alanı, Kemerkaya, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Order Akçaabat köfte at Komaroğlu Köfte Salonu
new.desc: A köfte house in Dürbinar, Akçaabat, serving the town's grilled Akçaabat köfte with piyaz and ayran.
new.tip: Eat it with ayran and piyaz; lunchtime is busy.
new.q: Komaroğlu Köfte Salonu, Orta Caddesi, Dürbinar, Akçaabat, Trabzon

new.title: Try kavurma pilav at Tarihi Kalkanoğlu Pilavcısı
new.desc: A rice shop at Pazarkapı run by the Kalkanoğlu family since 1856 and still sold by weight. The pilav is cooked in bone broth and butter and eaten with kavurma, kuru fasulye and apricot hoşaf.
new.tip: Go for lunch; it is a lunch-only institution.
new.q: Tarihi Kalkanoğlu Pilavcısı, Tophane Cami Sokak No:3, Pazarkapı, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Buy stone-oven Vakfıkebir bread at Rüştü'nün Fırını
new.desc: A bakery on Kalkanoğlu Caddesi at Pazarkapı that bakes the big round Vakfıkebir bread in a stone oven. The same oven turns out kıymalı pide.
new.tip: Buy the loaf warm; it is sold by weight.
new.q: Rüştü'nün Fırını, Kalkanoğlu Caddesi, Pazarkapı, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Eat round kıymalı pide at Çardak Pide
new.desc: A pide shop on Uzun Sokak known for the Trabzon-style round kıymalı pide and a triple kıyma-kavurma-peynir version.
new.tip: Ask for kıymalı yuvarlak pide with ayran.
new.q: Çardak Pide, Uzun Sokak, Kemerkaya, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Taste pistachio helva at Beton Helva
new.desc: Beton Helva is a Trabzon helva shop selling pistachio and other helva varieties, plus şıra, ice cream and sahlep.
new.tip: Buy a box to take home.
new.q: Beton Helva, Uzun Sokak, Gazipaşa, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Try Laz böreği at Nejla Hanım Ev Tatlıları
new.desc: A pastry shop on the Trabzon-Rize road at Yalıncak that has made Laz böreği, the custard-filled layered pastry, for over 20 years. It also sells baklava and chestnut cookies.
new.tip: Eat the Laz böreği warm or at room temperature.
new.q: Nejla Hanım Ev Tatlıları, Yalıncak Mahallesi, Trabzon Rize Yolu, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Eat muhlama at Asimer Kafe in Bostancı
new.desc: A garden breakfast hall in Bostancı popular for long weekend breakfasts with serpme and menemen, and a muhlama one reviewer called the best they had tried.
new.tip: Book for weekends; order muhlama with village bread.
new.q: Asimer Kafe ve Kahvaltı Salonu, Bostancı Mahallesi, Yılmaz Sokak, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Try mantı and pepeçura at Kalender Lokantası
new.desc: A home-style lokanta serving gözleme, mantı and desserts such as pepeçura.
new.tip: Go for lunch; the dishes change daily.
new.q: Kalender Lokantası, Cumhuriyet Mahallesi, Şehit Onur Fikret Dülger Caddesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Eat beef döner at Muharrem Usta
new.desc: A döner shop in Kemerkaya known for its beef döner.
new.tip: A quick lunch stop along Uzun Sokak.
new.q: Muharrem Usta, Hüsnü Aybay Sokak, Kemerkaya, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Pick up a kornet at Zemu Swiss Bakery
new.desc: A bakery in Erdoğdu listed by local guides for its kornet.
new.tip: Try it fresh in the morning.
new.q: Zemu Swiss Bakery, Manolya Sokak, Erdoğdu, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Eat copper-pan kuymak at Lermioğlu Konağı in Akçaabat
new.desc: A historic mansion in Akçaabat serving breakfast with kuymak in a copper pan, village bread, tulum cheese and jams.
new.tip: Reserve ahead.
new.q: Lermioğlu Konağı Bahçe Cafe, Sırt Sokak, Orta Mahalle, Akçaabat, Trabzon

new.title: Browse the Bedesten and old bazaar lanes
new.desc: The Trabzon Bedesten is one of the oldest structures in the centre, in the market quarter behind Meydan, with sections described as lower, middle and upper.
new.tip: Go in the morning when shops open.
new.q: Bedesten, Çarşı Mahallesi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Watch the hamsi at Trabzon Balık Pazarı
new.desc: The Balık Pazarı fish market in Ortahisar is busiest in the anchovy season, roughly September to April, when hamsi dominates the stalls beside whiting and horse mackerel.
new.tip: Go in the morning.
new.q: Trabzon Balık Pazarı, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Catch a Trabzonspor match at Papara Park
new.desc: Papara Park (Şenol Güneş Sports Complex) opened on 18 December 2016 with a capacity of about 40,980. It is the home of Trabzonspor.
new.tip: Tickets are sold through Passolig.
new.q: Papara Park, Şenol Güneş Spor Kompleksi, Ortahisar, Trabzon

new.title: Steam in Meydan Hamamı, a 300-year-old bathhouse
new.desc: Meydan Hamamı in Ortahisar is a roughly 300-year-old Ottoman bathhouse that reopened after a fire and renovation.
new.tip: Check opening hours and gender sessions.
new.q: Meydan Hamamı, Kemerkaya, Ortahisar, Trabzon
